file.content:
# Chapter 2 — Methods

## Study site

Twelve permanent transects run seaward from the high-water mark along the north headland. Each transect is marked with a stainless bolt at both ends and photographed on every visit.

## Sampling

Counts are taken at every low spring tide between March and September. Along each transect a 0.25 m² quadrat is placed at two-metre intervals. Inside each quadrat I count grazing snails (periwinkles and limpets) and estimate percentage algae cover by eye against a reference card.

## Grazing exclusion

Four transects carry mesh cages that keep snails out, so algae cover inside and outside a cage can be compared. Cages are scrubbed of fouling every second visit.

## Analysis

Snail density against algae cover is modelled per transect with a mixed model, tide height as a covariate.

# brewing log

Batch four started today. 1.2 kg of last summer's wildflower honey warmed in a pan of water, topped up to four litres, pitched with a sachet of dry wine yeast. Added a thumb of sliced ginger and the zest of one lemon because the ginger batch was the best one so far.

The airlock was bubbling about once a second by the evening. Demijohn sits in the corner of the kitchen away from the radiator. Plan to rack it off the lees in six weeks and bottle after eleven, same as last time.

# smoker checklist

Before every inspection:

- smoker cleaned of tar from last time, bellows not split
- fuel in the tin: burlap offcuts and a fist of dried pine needles, egg trays as a starter
- matches in the zip bag, not the lighter (it is out of gas)
- bucket of water next to the stand, filled

After: tip the embers into the bucket, never onto the grass. Cork the spout so it goes out.
